title: be- and ki-: Going In and Coming Out

sections.title: Two directions, glued onto verbs you already know
sections.content: be- ('in') and ki- ('out') are igekötők, verb prefixes, that attach directly onto megy ('go') and jön ('come') — the same two irregular verbs you already conjugate every day. bemegy means 'go in', bejön means 'come in', kimegy means 'go out', and kijön means 'come out'. The prefix just glues onto the front, and the verb behind it still conjugates exactly the way you already know.

items.english: Zsófia is coming into the room.
Károly is going out of the kitchen.

sections.content: The old megy/jön distinction still matters here: bemegy and kimegy describe motion away from the speaker (Meg is going in, seen from outside), while bejön and kijön describe motion toward the speaker (Meg is coming in, seen from inside). Pick the verb the way you already pick between megy and jön, and just prefix it.
